heading: Assert
text:
### Assert [IRET.19.1]

`ds_rete_wm_assert(engine, schema_id, slots, fact_out)`:

1. Determine the schema's identity key — the slots whose
   `identity_role` is KEY (IRET.4.1, [LFAC.1.7]). Search
   working memory for an existing fact of the same schema
   whose KEY-slot tuple matches exactly. Key = ∅ (no KEY
   slot) is a singleton: any existing fact of the schema
   matches. Key = all slots is a relation: only an identical
   tuple matches.
2. If found: compare the MUTABLE slots under per-slot
   tolerance rules (IRET.3.4) — the KEY slots already matched
   exactly. If all compare equal: suppress the assertion
   (no-op); set `*fact_out` to the existing fact; return
   `DS_OK`.
3. If found but a MUTABLE slot differs (update): retract the
   old fact (IRET.19.2), then fall through to insert.
4. Allocate a new `ds_rete_fact_t` with a fresh monotonic
   ID. Populate `assert_ns` with the held
   monotonic sample ([LTIM.2.8.6]).
5. For TTL-scoped schemas: set
   `deadline_ns = assert_ns + schema->default_ttl_ns`.
6. For logical-scoped schemas: initialise `justif_count = 0`.
7. For each alpha node registered for `schema_id`: evaluate
   all alpha tests against the new fact (IRET.6.4). On
   pass: insert the fact into the alpha memory and
   left-activate each downstream beta input.
8. Emit `DS_EV_FACT_ASSERT` stream event.
9. Set `*fact_out`; return `DS_OK`.

alloy.name: iret_19_1__identity_key
alloy.note: Step 1's key: the schema's KEY slots. The engine's ts carries ENGINE, so it is outside the key (RDSC.5.5.7, LFAC.9.1).

alloy.name: iret_19_1__key_and_payload_partition_slots
alloy.note: KEY and MUTABLE partition a logical schema's author slots, every slot but ts: assert matches on the one and compares the other. Bounded: six slots, six schemas.

alloy.name: iret_19_1__payload
alloy.note: Step 2's compared slots: the MUTABLE slots. The engine's ts carries ENGINE, so the no-op comparison leaves it out (LFAC.2.5.1).

alloy.name: iret_19_1__ts_outside_key_and_payload
alloy.note: A ts slot is in neither the key nor the payload assert reads, on every schema: no part in the match, no part in the comparison. Bounded: six slots, six schemas; fails if the partition's ENGINE line is dropped.

idris.name: iret_19_1__find_relation_nothing
idris.note: No match found means the value is not live.

idris.name: iret_19_1__emit_frame
idris.note: An assert of kind k changes no other kind's facts.

idris.name: iret_19_1__emit_shape
idris.note: A successful assert appends one fresh fact of the kind after removing at most one fact of the same kind (the entity replace).

idris.name: iret_19_1__entity_kind
idris.note: The entity match has the kind searched for.

idris.name: iret_19_1__relation_assert_shape
idris.note: A successful relation assert appended, and the value was not live before.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_fact
idris.note: Steps 1-4 for the three lifecycles the model has: key = all (relation) suppresses an identical tuple, key = one slot (entity) suppresses a same-payload reassert and otherwise retracts the old fact and inserts a fresh one, explicit always inserts. Not modelled: per-slot tolerance (step 2), TTL deadlines (5), `justif_count` (6), alpha evaluation (7), stream events (8).

idris.name: iret_19_1__find_entity
idris.note: Step 1 for a one-slot key: the live fact with that key.

idris.name: iret_19_1__find_relation
idris.note: Step 1 for key = all slots: only an identical tuple matches.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert
idris.note: ASSERT under the kind's lifecycle, exactly as Rete/FireLoop.idr's `iret_19_1__assert_fact` decides it: a no-op reassertion changes nothing (steps 1-2); a meaningful change retracts the old fact then inserts the new one, whose id was chosen while the old was live (step 3, [LFAC.2.5.3]); step 7's 'left-activate' is read as right-activation, since the step feeds an alpha memory, a join's right input.

idris.name: iret_19_1__insert
idris.note: Insert a fresh fact: append to working memory, then dispatch to every alpha in order.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_unique
idris.note: Assert keeps one live fact per key on every path.

idris.name: iret_19_1__entity_key
idris.note: The entity an assert finds has the key asked for.

idris.name: iret_19_1__find_entity_nothing
idris.note: When an assert finds no entity, no live fact has the kind and key.

idris.name: iret_19_1__insert_unique
idris.note: Inserting a fact fresh for its kind's lifecycle keeps one live fact per key.

idris.name: iret_7_9_2__acquire
idris.note: The insert of a fresh fact leaves no activation whose NOT node the fact satisfies.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_view
idris.note: ASSERT UNDER THE LIFECYCLE keeps the view: a no-op changes nothing, an insert is of a fresh fact, and a replace retracts a live fact then inserts a fresh one.

idris.name: iret_19_1__insert_view
idris.note: Inserting a fresh fact keeps the view.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_ordered
idris.note: ASSERT UNDER THE LIFECYCLE keeps the order: a no-op changes nothing, an insert is of a fresh fact, and a replace retracts a live fact then inserts a fresh one.

idris.name: iret_19_1__insert_ordered
idris.note: Inserting a fresh fact keeps the order.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_g
idris.note: Assert with the set beside it.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_r
idris.note: The set through assert, path by path as the clause decides them.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_sound
idris.note: ASSERT UNDER THE LIFECYCLE keeps the ghost sound: a suppressed reassertion changes neither engine nor set; every other path changes working memory and clears the set.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__record_action
idris.note: Step 4's `assert_ns` from the held monotonic sample, for an emit: the net's clock at the firing. LESS than the clause: the stamp alone; the rest of the assert is Rete/NetworkTtl.idr's and Rete/FireLoop.idr's.

idris.name: ltac_3_3__explicit_mint_is_stamped
idris.note: Step 4's mint, stamped with the held sample, for the explicit lifecycle.

idris.name: ltac_3_3__stamp_is_fire_at
idris.note: A fact the parent's firing mints is stamped with the held sample (step 4), through the stamped RHS's record of the emit.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_state_just
idris.note: The named assert-then-propagate, when the assert changed working memory.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_state
idris.note: FireLoop's assert under the kind's lifecycle, then one propagation when working memory changed: what the Emit action and the asserted input both do, named so that a statement can mention it.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__assert_agree
idris.note: ASSERT UNDER THE LIFECYCLE keeps the agreement: the network's assert and FireLoop's assert-then-propagate decide alike on the same working memory -- fresh insert, suppressed no-op, or retract-and-replace.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__insert_agree
idris.note: INSERTING A FRESH FACT keeps the agreement, against FireLoop's one propagation over the grown working memory.

idris.name: iret_19_1__insert_flags
idris.note: INSERTING A FRESH FACT: every activation afterwards is an old one or unfired, and every old activation whose match survives is still there, flag and all -- an assertion creates only matches holding the new fact, so no old match is created anew.

idris.name: iret_19_1__assert_fact_shape
idris.note: What an assert that changes working memory produces: the fresh wrapper appended to working memory, or to working memory less the entity it replaces.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__well_assert
idris.note: The assert keeps the state well-formed: fresh insert or retract-and-replace.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__well_grow
idris.note: The fresh insert keeps the state well-formed.

idris.name: iret_19_1__emit_core
idris.note: A successful assert: the invariant holds after propagation, and the change keeps ids identifying, adds only the new fact -- whose id is fresh and unbound -- and keeps ids unique. Append and entity replace alike.
